judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's recomputations are correct: (x+4)^2+(y-7)^2 = 36 gives centre (-4,7) and r = 6; Dev's circle gives centre (5,-2) and r = 7 against his (-5,2) and 49; semi-axes 5 and 3; x^2+y^2-6x+10y+18 = 0 completes to (x-3)^2+(y+5)^2 = 16 so centre (3,-5) and r = 4; Rae's ellipse has a vertical major axis of full length 2*7 = 14; the shifted ellipse has centre (-3,1) and semi-major 4; Sam's hyperbola opens up and down with vertices (0,+-3). The judge's count observation is the odd one: it defends against a 'machine count warning' that observations/curr-399.json does not contain (declared_problem_count 8, problem_count_matches true, capture_problems []). More substantively, the judge scored instruction_following 4/4 and I cannot support that. This is a misconception sheet whose find-and-fix items ask for the diagnosis IN WORDS - problem 2 'Dev made two separate errors. Name each one'; problem 5 'State which denominator decides the major axis and why'; problem 7 'Which term carries the plus sign, and what does that tell you about the direction the branches open?' - and the answer key prints an explicit rubric for each ('Full-credit answer says: ...' on pages 1, 3 and 3), which is proof the author treated them as graded prose. verify.json records no manual entry for 2, 5 or 7; the only manual item is problem 8, and final_response.md states 'What is flagged for manual review. Problem 8 only.' The categorical answers those problems also request - the corrected DIRECTION, vertical for problem 5 and up-and-down for problem 7 - are likewise absent from verify.json, so the Quick Answers bank prints '5. 14' and '7. -3, 3, 3' with no direction at all. Also: unlike eight of the ten cases in this batch, final_response.md never names a PDF filename.

strengths_to_preserve: The trap declarations are unusually complete and each one names a distinct step rather than a generic 'wrong answer': twelve traps across seven problems, including problem 5's pair (4 = took the denominator under x^2 because it is written first; 7 = stopped at the semi-axis without doubling) and problem 6's pair (16 = denominator used raw; 2 = the smaller denominator, i.e. the semi-MINOR axis). The key's note on problem 5 then grades the wrong answers by severity: 'the reported 4 ... wrong axis, no square root and no doubling, three errors in one number.'

Centres are verified as the SOLUTION of the binomials set to zero (verify.json ids 1, 2 and 6 use a system on ['x + 4', 'y - 7'] and so on), which mirrors exactly the method the sheet teaches and the directions demand - 'Show the step where you set the binomial to zero' - instead of verifying a number that the student would obtain a different way.

Problem 7's key separates the two independent errors in Sam's claim: the direction (decided by which term carries the plus sign, 'the subtracted term never touches the curve') and the vertex distance (taken from the wrong denominator), and closes with why the wrong answer is not merely off but nonsensical - 'It would place vertices where the hyperbola has no points at all.'

Problem 8 is a well-built open construction: one student-chosen non-origin centre used for a circle, an ellipse with a vertical major axis and a hyperbola opening left and right, plus an explanation of how a reader tells them apart. The manual desc lists the three things a full-credit answer must contain, and the key supplies a complete model at centre (2,-5).

root_causes.description: SKILL.md routes error-analysis explicitly through the ordinary check types - 'error-analysis ("find and fix the mistake") via the ordinary types - the planted wrong result is checkably wrong and the correction checkably right' - while a separate line reserves manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer'. On a misconception sheet the two rules collide, and the first wins: the corrected NUMBER is verified and the requested NAMING of the error is recorded nowhere.
evidence: SKILL.md line 249 (error-analysis via ordinary types) against line 257 (manual for any explanation/reasoning answer).
worksheet.pdf problems 2, 5 and 7 each request a named diagnosis; verify.json ids 2, 5 and 7 contain only eval/solve/system entries.
answer_key.pdf prints 'Full-credit answer says:' rubrics for exactly those three problems - the author knew they were graded prose.
final_response.md: 'What is flagged for manual review. Problem 8 only.'

root_causes.description: Categorical corrections have no representation in the contract, so the direction answers that these find-and-fix items exist to correct are neither checked nor flagged. Problem 5's answer is 'vertical, length 14' and only 14 is recorded; problem 7's answer is 'opens up and down, vertices (0,+-3)' and only the vertex numbers are recorded.
evidence: worksheet.pdf p.3 problem 5 ('give the correct direction and the correct full length') and p.4 problem 7 ('Correct both the direction and the vertices').
verify.json id 5 = one eval -> 14; id 7 = solve -> [-3, 3] plus eval -> 3.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '5. 14' and '7. -3, 3, 3' - no direction, and the trailing 3 is unlabelled.

root_causes.description: final_response.md describes the three documents but gives no filename or path for any of them, so the reader cannot map the description to a built artifact. Eight of the ten cases in this batch print the ws_/ak_/ss_ names.
evidence: final_response.md contains no .pdf token anywhere; it opens 'Three PDFs are ready: the student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a two-page study guide.'
gate_log.txt prints the three built paths, so the information was available at delivery time.

improvements.title: A find-and-fix item that asks the student to NAME the error needs a manual entry beside its numeric checks
improvements.proposed_change: Resolve the contradiction in SKILL.md directly: keep 'error-analysis via the ordinary types' for the corrected VALUE, and add that when the stem also asks the student to name, state or explain the error, the same id carries a manual entry whose desc holds the acceptance criterion. Problems 2, 5 and 7 here each need one, and the text can be lifted verbatim from the key's existing 'Full-credit answer says:' lines.
improvements.regression_test: Advisory lint in scripts/verify.py (exit 2): for each id, if the worksheet stem matches /name (each|the) (one|error)|state which .* and why|explain|what does that tell you/ and no manual entry exists under that id, warn with the id and matched phrase. Assert it fires on curr-399 problems 2, 5 and 7 and stays silent on problems 1, 3, 4 and 6.
improvements.expected_impact: Misconception-analysis sheets - a whole instructional mode in this curriculum - stop reporting that everything but the last problem was machine-graded when half the requested response is prose.
improvements.risk: Sheets whose find-and-fix items really are numeric-only would see spurious warnings; keeping the lint advisory rather than a hard gate contains that.

improvements.title: Record the corrected DIRECTION on problems 5 and 7, not only the corrected number
improvements.proposed_change: Move the contract to one check-or-manual-entry per printed answer slot, enforced in tests/check_answer_key.py, and give categorical answers a home - a closed-vocabulary "choice" check type ({"type": "choice", "expected": "vertical", "from": ["horizontal", "vertical"]}) that verify.py compares as a plain string and the bank prints verbatim. Problem 5 then reads 'vertical, 14' and problem 7 'opens up and down, vertices (0, +-3)' in the Quick Answers bank instead of '14' and '-3, 3, 3'.
improvements.regression_test: Two tests. (a) check_answer_key.py fails a fixture whose problem segment boxes both a direction word and a number against a verify id with a single numeric entry - it passes today. (b) A "choice" entry with expected 'vertical' renders as 'vertical' in the bank and fails verification when the key boxes 'horizontal'.
improvements.expected_impact: On a sheet whose declared focus is diagnosing sign and denominator errors, the corrected orientation - the thing Rae and Sam actually got wrong - stops being absent from both the verification data and the grading bank.
improvements.risk: A new check type widens the schema; keep it a literal string compare against a declared closed vocabulary so it introduces no evaluation surface.

improvements.title: Name the three built PDFs by filename in final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: Make it a delivery requirement in SKILL.md that final_response.md lists each artifact by the filename build.sh printed in its gate summary, rather than describing them generically. Eight of the ten cases in this batch already do so; this one and curr-381 do not.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/check_artifact_health.py (or the eval delivery check) to fail when final_response.md contains no ws_*.pdf, ak_*.pdf and ss_*.pdf token. curr-399's current final_response.md fails; it passes once the filenames are listed.
improvements.expected_impact: The reader can connect each described document to a file without re-reading the build log.
improvements.risk: Filenames drift on rebuild; generate the list from the gate summary rather than typing it by hand.

case_summary: Eight tightly focused conic error-analysis problems, all mathematically correct on recomputation, with twelve declared traps that each name a distinct wrong step rather than a generic slip, centres verified the same way the sheet teaches them (solving the binomials for zero), and a well-specified open construction in problem 8. Where it falls short of 32/32 is the handling of the written half. Problems 2, 5 and 7 explicitly ask the student to NAME the error, and the answer key prints a 'Full-credit answer says:' rubric for each - yet verify.json declares no manual entry for any of them and final_response.md states that problem 8 is the only manual item, on a sheet whose whole instructional mode is diagnosis. The categorical corrections those items request (major axis vertical; branches open up and down) are similarly unrecorded, so the Quick Answers bank offers '5. 14' and '7. -3, 3, 3' with the direction - the actual misconception - missing. Delivery is also thinner than its siblings: no PDF filename appears in final_response.md.
